question: How did Raja Rammohan Roy contribute to the movement against the practice of Sati in early 19th-century Bengal?

options.text: He organized armed protests in Bengal villages
He issued government ordinances against orthodox leaders
He campaigned using newspapers and engaged in debates
He formed alliances with British Christian missionaries

solution:
The correct answer is __**He campaigned using newspapers and engaged in debates**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Raja Rammohan Roy** played a pivotal role in abolishing the practice of Sati (widow immolation) during the early 19th century in Bengal.
 
• He used newspapers and journals such as **‘Sambad Kaumudi’** to educate the masses and highlight the evils of Sati.
 
• Rammohan Roy engaged in debates and dialogues with orthodox Hindu leaders and British officials, advocating for social reform and raising awareness about the cruelty and religious misinterpretation related to Sati.
 
• He presented reasoned arguments and petitions to the British government, which culminated in the **Sati Regulation Act of 1829** under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.
 
• His efforts were instrumental in fostering a progressive mindset in society, paving the way for the eradication of practices rooted in superstition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abolition of Sati**

 
 
• The practice of Sati involved the immolation of widows on the funeral pyres of their husbands, and it was deeply rooted in societal and religious traditions in India.
 
• Rammohan Roy’s efforts played a crucial role in the enactment of the **Sati Regulation Act of 1829**, which prohibited the practice and made it illegal.
 
• His work is considered a landmark in the history of social reform in India, symbolizing the shift towards modernity and human rights.
